requirement:
`languages::Yaml` implements `OutlineLang` under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider`. Its default value is
cheaply cloneable and claims `.yml` and `.yaml`.
Filename-based constructors select it under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults`.
rationale:
The marked test `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline]` covers every obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.language`. It carries a {test} reference to the requirement and calls the generic `check` helper with `languages::Yaml`.

- **Implements `OutlineLang`:** `check` is bound by `L: OutlineLang + Default + Copy`, so the code compiles only if `Yaml` implements the trait. It also calls `name()`, `outline()`, `fingerprint_scheme()` and `search_structure()` on it. `name()` is only checked to be non-empty, and `outline()` is checked through the root span and the selectors.
- **Default value:** `L::default().fingerprint_scheme()` is asserted to equal `"yaml-structural-v1"`.
- **Cheaply cloneable:** `size_of::<L>()` is asserted to be 0, so cloning cannot allocate or copy configuration. `Clone::clone` is also called, and the clone is checked to report the same extensions.
- **Claims `.yml` and `.yaml`:** `extensions()` is asserted to equal `&["yml","yaml"]` exactly. That fixes both the set and the omission of the leading dot.
- **Filename-based constructors select it:** the test builds `OutlineContent::from_source` with `a.YAML` and with `not-present.YML` and `not-present.YAML`, one for each claimed extension in upper case. For each it asserts that the fingerprint equals the explicit-Yaml fingerprint, and that `select("pair[check]")` succeeds. That selector exists only in the YAML outline. A plain-text fallback would give line-based selectors, so the test would catch a wrong selection. Using upper-case extensions also exercises the case-insensitive matching in `requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults`.

The test never uses a lower-case filename. Matching an exact lower-case extension is the baseline behavior of the matching the upper-case cases already exercise, so I don't count this as a gap.

The cited `language_provider` and `defaults` requirements are context only. Their application to YAML is exercised by the same test.

text: `OutlineLang` defines the language interface. Each implementation supplies its
name, claimed extensions, and outlining operation. Cloning a language shares
its prepared configuration instead of rebuilding it or copying it in proportion
to its size. Its result uses the public items, spans, and hashes under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.items`. Filename extensions omit the leading dot.
The filename-based constructors include Rust, Python, TypeScript, TSX,
Markdown, CSS, TOML, and YAML languages. Extension matching is
case-insensitive, using each implementation's claimed extensions.
A filename without a claimed extension uses the
